prompt.adult: Paul wrote that he had been crucified with Christ and that Christ lives in him. By what does he say he now lives?
prompt.child: Paul says his old life was crucified with Christ, and now Christ lives in him. How does Paul say he lives now?
prompt.teen: In Galatians 2:20, Paul says it is no longer he who lives, but Christ in him. How does he live the life he now lives?
prompt.older: According to Galatians 2:20, by what does Paul live the life he now lives?

choices.text: Faith in the Son of God
The strength of his own will
Keeping every rule of the law

verses.text: I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.

explanation.adult: Galatians 2:20 says how Paul lives the life he now lives. Read the words after "I live by."
explanation.child: Look near the end of Galatians 2:20 for the words "I live by." Read what comes next.
explanation.teen: Find "I live by" in Galatians 2:20; the answer follows, and it names whom Paul trusts.
explanation.older: The phrase following "I live by" in 2:20 identifies the means; the verse then describes that One as having loved Paul.

teaching.extended_explanation: Paul describes a life that now belongs to Christ. Galatians 2:20 also says Christ loved him and gave Himself for him. Read the words after "I live by" to see how Paul lives.
teaching.takeaway: Paul lives by faith in the Son of God, who loved him and gave Himself for him.

prompt.adult: Which of these is part of the fruit of the Spirit listed in Galatians 5:22?
prompt.child: Paul lists good things the Holy Spirit grows in a believer's life. Which of these is on his list?
prompt.teen: Paul names the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22. Which of these choices is one of them?
prompt.older: Galatians 5:22 begins Paul's list of the fruit of the Spirit. Which of the following appears in that verse?

verses.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,

explanation.adult: Galatians 5:22 lists seven qualities. Compare each choice with the list.
explanation.child: Read the list in Galatians 5:22 slowly. Only one choice is in it.
explanation.teen: Check each choice against the list after "the fruit of the Spirit is."
explanation.older: Match the choices against the seven nouns in 5:22.

teaching.extended_explanation: Paul contrasts sinful works with the fruit of the Spirit. The fruit is a list of qualities, not possessions or reputation. Read the list in 5:22 and look for the choice that matches.
teaching.takeaway: Longsuffering is part of the fruit of the Spirit.

prompt.adult: Paul's list of the fruit of the Spirit continues into Galatians 5:23. What is the last quality he names?
prompt.child: Paul's list of the fruit of the Spirit ends in Galatians 5:23. What is the very last one?
prompt.teen: What is the final item in Paul's list of the fruit of the Spirit?
prompt.older: According to Galatians 5:23, which quality closes the list of the fruit of the Spirit?

verses.text: gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.

explanation.adult: Galatians 5:23 begins with the last two items of the list. Read the second one.
explanation.child: Read the beginning of Galatians 5:23. The list ends right before the first period.
explanation.teen: 5:23 starts with two qualities, then says "Against such there is no law." You need the one just before that sentence.
explanation.older: The list finishes in the opening words of 5:23, ahead of the remark about the law.

teaching.extended_explanation: The fruit of the Spirit begins in 5:22 and finishes in 5:23. Paul then adds that no law stands against such things. Read the opening words of 5:23 for the last quality.
teaching.takeaway: The last quality in the fruit of the Spirit is self-control.

prompt.adult: Paul says to walk in the Spirit. What does he say you then will not fulfill?
prompt.child: Paul tells believers to walk in the Spirit. If they do, what will they not give in to?
prompt.teen: In Galatians 5:16 Paul gives a command and a result. If you walk in the Spirit, what will you not fulfill?
prompt.older: According to Galatians 5:16, walking in the Spirit means one will not fulfill what?

verses.text: I say then: Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh.

explanation.adult: Galatians 5:16 has a command and a promise. Read the promise after "and you shall not fulfill."
explanation.teen: The result in 5:16 comes after "you shall not fulfill."
explanation.older: The second clause of 5:16 names what is left unfulfilled; 5:17 explains the conflict behind it.

teaching.extended_explanation: Paul says the Spirit and our sinful desires pull against each other. Galatians 5:16 shows what happens when a believer walks in the Spirit. Read the last part of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the lust of the flesh.

prompt.adult: Paul tells believers to bear one another's burdens. What does he say they fulfill by doing so?
prompt.child: Paul says to help carry each other's heavy loads. What do believers fulfill when they do that?
prompt.teen: According to Galatians 6:2, carrying each other's burdens fulfills what?
prompt.older: In Galatians 6:2, what is fulfilled when believers bear one another's burdens?

verses.text: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

explanation.adult: Galatians 6:2 has a command and then a result. Read the words after "and so fulfill."
explanation.teen: Find "and so fulfill" in 6:2. The answer comes next.
explanation.older: The final phrase of 6:2 names what is fulfilled; compare 5:14 on love fulfilling the law.

teaching.extended_explanation: Helping others carry their burdens is a way of living out what Jesus taught. Galatians 6:2 names what believers fulfill this way. Read the end of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Bearing one another's burdens fulfills the law of Christ.

prompt.adult: Paul tells believers not to grow weary while doing good. What does he promise will happen in due season if they do not lose heart?
prompt.child: Paul says not to get tired of doing good. What will happen at the right time if we don't give up?
prompt.teen: Galatians 6:9 encourages people who are tired of doing good. What does it promise in due season?
prompt.older: According to Galatians 6:9, what will happen in due season to those who do not lose heart?

verses.text: And let us not grow weary while doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart.

explanation.adult: Galatians 6:9 gives a promise after the word "for." Read that part of the verse.
explanation.child: Look at the second half of Galatians 6:9.
explanation.teen: The promise in 6:9 comes after "for in due season."
explanation.older: The second clause of 6:9 continues the harvest image from 6:7-8.

teaching.extended_explanation: Paul has been using a farming picture of sowing. In 6:9 he encourages believers to keep doing good and gives a promise for those who do not lose heart. Read the words after "in due season."
teaching.takeaway: In due season we shall reap if we do not lose heart.

prompt.adult: Paul warns about believers who bite and devour one another. What does he say they should beware of?
prompt.child: Paul warns about people who attack each other with harsh words and actions, like animals biting. What does he say could happen to them?
prompt.teen: According to Galatians 5:15, what danger comes from biting and devouring each other?
prompt.older: In Galatians 5:15, what outcome does Paul warn of for those who bite and devour one another?

verses.text: But if you bite and devour one another, beware lest you be consumed by one another!

explanation.adult: Galatians 5:15 ends with a warning after "beware lest you be." Read those last words.
explanation.teen: The warning in 5:15 follows "beware lest you be."
explanation.older: The lest-clause at the close of 5:15 states the result of mutual biting and devouring.

teaching.extended_explanation: Right after saying the whole law is fulfilled in loving your neighbor, Paul warns about the opposite. Galatians 5:15 shows where constant attacks on each other lead. Read the end of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Those who bite and devour one another risk being consumed by one another.

prompt.adult: Galatians 5:13 says believers are called to liberty but should not use it as a chance to please themselves. What should they do with it instead, which 5:14 ties to the whole law?
prompt.child: Paul says God has set believers free. But freedom is not for doing whatever you want. What does Paul say to do instead?
prompt.teen: Freedom isn't a license to please yourself. What does Galatians 5:13 say love should lead believers to do, and how does 5:14 back it up?
prompt.older: Read Galatians 5:13 with 5:14. How should believers use their liberty, given that the whole law is fulfilled in loving one's neighbor?

verses.text: For you, brethren, have been called to liberty; only do not use liberty as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
For all the law is fulfilled in one word, even in this: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”

explanation.adult: Galatians 5:13 ends with what believers should do through love. Galatians 5:14 then quotes the command that sums up the law.
explanation.child: Read the end of Galatians 5:13, after "through love."
explanation.teen: 5:13 gives the right use of freedom in its last phrase; 5:14 shows why that fits the law.
explanation.older: The final clause of 5:13, after "through love," is the alternative Paul gives; 5:14 grounds it in the command to love one's neighbor.

teaching.extended_explanation: Paul has argued that believers are free. In 5:13 he guards that freedom from being misused, and in 5:14 he shows that the whole law is fulfilled in one command about loving your neighbor. Read the end of 5:13 to see what love leads believers to do.
teaching.takeaway: Believers are free, and through love they should serve one another.
